coverage.draytek: Vigor routers embed a CWMP client. GetParameterValues, SetParameterValues, Download and Reboot are driven from here.

headline.partial: {{brand}} is only partly covered by the ACS.

coverage.intro: TR-069 is one transport among five, not the architecture. The ACS reaches the brands whose firmware ships a CWMP client — and two of the four do not.
coverage.mikrotik: RouterOS ships no TR-069 client at all. This is not a missing integration — the software has no CWMP agent to talk to.
coverage.mikrotikInstead: MikroTik is driven over the RouterOS API and SSH, which is the richer path anyway.
coverage.sonicwall: SonicOS ships no TR-069 client. SonicWall is managed through its REST API.
coverage.sonicwallInstead: Use the SonicOS REST transport declared on the device.
coverage.title: Brand coverage
coverage.unknownBrand: This device has no brand recorded, so no coverage statement can be made.
coverage.zyxel: Only the xDSL/GPON CPE range (VMG, DX, EX) is TR-069. USG FLEX, ATP and Nebula-managed gear are reached over REST or SSH and never appear on this screen.
coverage.zyxelFamilyHint: This device is in family {{family}}, which is not the TR-069 CPE range.
coverage.zyxelInstead: For USG FLEX / ATP / Nebula, use the configuration and change screens.

body.armed: A restore script and a start-up scheduler are on the equipment. If we lose it, it comes back on its own.
body.disarmed: The dead-man has been removed and confirmed gone. The equipment carries no scheduler that would revert this change.
body.fired: The equipment restored itself to its pre-change configuration. The change did not stick; the site did.
body.not_armed: Nothing has been installed on the box yet. Until the dead-man is armed, this change has no automatic recovery.
body.soaking: The change is applied and verified, and it is being watched. The dead-man is STILL armed throughout.

deadman.disarmedNote: The change will survive a reboot from now on.
deadman.downgraded: The net actually obtained is WEAKER than the one planned. Read this before you close the laptop.
deadman.stillArmedWarning: While the dead-man is armed, the equipment will REVERT this change at its next reboot. The job is not finished until it has been disarmed.

change.degradedConfirmedBody: This equipment had no automatic recovery, and an operator confirmed that explicitly before launch.

killSwitch.buttonHint: Refuses every write to every equipment, immediately.
killSwitch.engageBody: Every change job is refused from the moment you confirm, on every equipment in scope. Nothing is written, nothing is undone: it stops the queue, it does not touch a router.
killSwitch.engagedBody: The {{scope}} kill switch is engaged. Every change job is refused.

killSwitch.unavailable: This build does not serve the kill switch.
killSwitch.unknownBody: The state could not be read. It is treated as engaged, because a kill switch that fails open is not a kill switch. This is not a report that somebody stopped the world.

override.attribution: This override will be recorded under:
override.attributionHint: The database refuses an override with no named human and no timestamp. It is not a convention, it is a constraint.
override.blindHint: These are not warnings. They are the parts of the configuration we did not model.
override.blindTitle: What the guard could not read
override.blockBody: This is not the apply button. It bypasses the protection that stands between this plan and losing remote access to a customer site.
override.blockHint: It requires a written reason, it names you in the database, and it stays visible on this job forever.
override.consequence: If this refusal is right, the site loses remote administration and the repair is a van.
override.degradedAlso: This equipment also has no automatic recovery. Typing the name confirms both facts.
override.finalAudit: Your name, this reason and this timestamp stay on the job permanently.

finalBullet.ACCEPT: The guard cleared this plan — you should not be here.
finalBullet.INDETERMINATE: You are ignoring the fact that the guard could not conclude.
finalBullet.NOT_RUN: You are applying a plan no guard examined.
finalBullet.REJECT: You are ignoring a proof that this change cuts the management path.

finalNet.ARMED: If it goes wrong, the equipment repairs itself at the next reboot.
finalNet.ARMED_BY_PEER: If it goes wrong, a neighbouring MikroTik must repair it — and it must still be reachable.
finalNet.DEGRADED: If it goes wrong, NOTHING repairs it. Somebody drives to the site.

override.finalTitle: Last screen. After this, the job is queued.
override.noCapability: The guard did not clear this plan. Your account may not override a guard verdict, so there is nothing more to do here — recompile after fixing the plan, or ask somebody who holds that permission.
override.noReasons: No reason was recorded. That is worse, not better: nothing tells you what you are overriding.
override.proofsHint: Each line names the record and the plan operation that produced it.
override.reasonHint: A real sentence. "ok" and "asap" are refused, here and in the database.
override.reasonIntro: Write why. This sentence is stored with the job, shown to whoever reads it afterwards, and it is what an incident review will start from.
override.reasonPlaceholder: e.g. Concentrator migration; the tunnel moves to l2tp-mgmt2, validated with the customer and a technician is on site.

whatYouOverride.ACCEPT: The guard cleared this plan. There is nothing to override.
whatYouOverride.INDETERMINATE: You are about to override an admission of blindness. The guard could not conclude, and the part of the model it could not read is exactly where a lockout rule would live.
whatYouOverride.NOT_RUN: You are about to apply a plan no guard examined. Nothing checked whether this change cuts the tunnel.
whatYouOverride.REJECT: You are about to override a PROOF. The forwarding engine walked your target configuration and found the management packet denied.

change.overrideTitle: This job was pushed past a guard refusal
change.rolledBackBody: The dead-man fired and the configuration on the box is the pre-change one. The change did not stick; the site did. This is the safety machinery working.

body.ARMED: A restore script and a start-up scheduler are installed on the box before the change. If the change cuts our access, the router reverts to its previous configuration at the next reboot, on its own.
body.ARMED_BY_PEER: The dead-man is carried by a MikroTik on the same site, reached over a tunnel this change does not touch. One brand repairs another.
body.DEGRADED: We will know that this equipment stopped reporting. We will not be able to do anything about it remotely.

errors.deviceRequired: Pick the device this threshold applies to.
errors.forMax: The dwell time cannot exceed 24 hours.
errors.forPositive: The dwell time must be greater than zero. A threshold that fires on the first sample is exactly what produces alert storms.
errors.groupRequired: Pick the group this threshold applies to.
errors.interfaceRequired: Pick the interface this threshold applies to.

explainer.for: The condition must hold without interruption for this long before anybody is notified. Without it, a single 30-second spike wakes the on-call engineer. This is the setting that turns a transient into a non-event.
explainer.hysteresis: Once the alert is firing, the value must come back this far past the threshold before it clears. Without it, a value parked on the boundary fires, clears, fires and clears again on every polling cycle, forever.
explainer.mandatory: Both fields are mandatory and carry no default: the database refuses a threshold that omits them, on purpose. A value you did not choose is a value nobody can explain during an incident.
explainer.title: Dwell time and hysteresis — the two settings that stop alert storms

hints.forSeconds: How long the condition must hold before the alert fires. Below the polling interval it has no effect; two polling cycles is a sensible starting point.
hints.hysteresis: Expressed as a percentage of the threshold value. 10 % on a threshold of 80 % means the alert clears below 72 %.
hints.hysteresisZero: With no hysteresis, a value sitting exactly on the threshold will fire and clear on every polling cycle.

thresholds.metricAppliesDevice: Device metric — evaluated once per device.
thresholds.metricAppliesInterface: Interface metric — evaluated on every interface in scope.

preview.clears: It clears once the value comes back {{comparator}} {{value}} — {{pct}} % past the threshold.
preview.clearsNoHysteresis: It clears as soon as the value is {{comparator}} {{value}}, with no margin at all.
preview.fires: It fires when the value stays {{comparator}} {{value}} for {{duration}}.
preview.title: In plain language
